issues.legal_issue: A landlord seeking possession for a bona fide need to start a business must plead the precise nature of the intended business.
material_facts: The landlords pleaded that they had no other means of livelihood and wanted to start their own business in the premises, which they said were suitable for that purpose.
They also pleaded that they had no other building for the purpose and could not afford to hire a similar building.
The trial court decreed ejectment on the ground of bona fide requirement.
The High Court reversed the decree because the landlords had not specified the nature of the business they intended to start.
issues.conclusion: The landlords were not required to plead the precise nature of the business. The High Court’s judgment was set aside and the trial court’s judgment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: In a claim for possession based on a landlord’s bona fide requirement to start a business, it is not necessary to plead the precise nature of that business. Even if the landlord identifies a particular business, the landlord cannot be bound to start that same business after obtaining possession. The judgment relies on no provision or earlier case.

predicates.ejectment_suit_for_bona_fide_business_ne: The landlords brought an ejectment suit asserting that they needed the premises to start a business.
predicates.landlords_pleaded_intention_to_start_own: The landlords pleaded that they intended to start their own business in the premises.
predicates.landlords_pleaded_no_other_means_of_live: The landlords pleaded that they had no other means of livelihood.
predicates.landlords_pleaded_premises_suitable_and_: The landlords pleaded that the premises were suitable and that they had no other building available for the business.

issues.definition: When landlords seek ejectment to start their own business and plead their lack of livelihood and suitable alternatives, their pleading is sufficient without specifying the type of business.
